rationale: The sources give the standard definitions of refinement, local finiteness, point-finiteness, and star refinement. The item combines them into one convention ledger and uses a point-star notation rather than reproducing one source verbatim; the mathematical notions and directions agree.

Rice topology notes §5.13.2 state that closures of a locally finite family remain locally finite and that closure commutes with its union; the closed-union conclusion is the stated specialization. The local proof expands the standard neighbourhood argument in different prose.
The notes use exactly the library convention: every open cover has a locally finite open refining cover, with Hausdorffness not built into the definition.
The source states under the same non-Hausdorff convention that every compact space is paracompact. The proof is the standard finite-subcover argument, rewritten locally.
Munkres §41, Theorem 41.2, states exactly that every closed subspace of a paracompact space is paracompact. The item supplies the usual ambient-cover/traces proof in local notation.

The topology notes from California State University, Northridge (CSUN) prove that a paracompact Hausdorff space is regular by the same locally finite refinement and closure-of-union construction. The item separates Hausdorffness from the local paracompactness convention and rewrites the proof.
Munkres §41, Theorem 41.1, states exactly that every paracompact Hausdorff space is normal. The proof is a standard closed-set separation argument adapted to the library's separate regularity lemma.

The sources define partitions by continuous [0,1]-valued functions summing to one with locally finite supports and define subordination by support containment. The item instead requires local finiteness of cozero sets; for such a family the closure lemma makes the support family locally finite, and the converse is immediate. This is an equivalent convention delta.

The university sources record continuity of arithmetic operations on real-valued continuous maps; absolute value and binary max/min follow by the displayed standard formulas, finite nonempty versions by iteration, and division is restricted to the nonzero-denominator subspace. The item merges these established closure rules into one statement and supplies its own epsilon proof.

Rice §5.14.1 gives the same locally finite-sum theorem for arbitrary continuous real-valued functions. The item specializes to nonnegative functions whose cozero family is locally finite and rewrites the identical local finite-sum argument.

Rice §5.14.2 gives the same positive locally finite family, continuous sum, normalization psi_l=phi_l/Phi, unchanged positivity sets, and sum-one conclusion. The item adds the immediate support-equality consequence and uses the library's cozero terminology.

The sources give the shrinking lemma and the iterated chain of locally finite covers with closure containment. The item exposes the normally implicit Choice used to retain cover assignments and reindexes the two applications, so it is a faithful semantic alteration rather than an exact transcription.

Both sources prove existence of a subordinate partition on a paracompact Hausdorff space by shrinking, Urysohn functions, a locally finite positive sum, and normalization. The item makes Choice and Dependent Choice explicit and uses cozero-local-finiteness, which are convention/foundational deltas.

Robbin states that a Hausdorff space admits partitions subordinate to every open cover iff it is paracompact. The item makes the sufficient Choice/DC assumptions explicit and uses the equivalent locally finite cozero convention; its reverse proof extracts the cozero refinement.

The sources give finite-cover partitions on normal spaces and the relabel-and-sum construction that groups a locally finite partition over a finite target cover. Compact Hausdorff implies normal in the standard setting; the item makes Choice/DC explicit and packages the result as a compact-Hausdorff corollary.

Ornstein's primary two-page paper, part (A), constructs from a well-ordered metric open cover the same dyadic-ball point-finite open refinement. The item modernizes notation, makes Choice explicit, and expands the coverage and ordinal-descent checks.

Ornstein's part (B) starts with the point-finite cover from part (A), assigns controlled-radius balls to first eligible members, and proves local finiteness by the same small-ball test. The item separates the upgrade as a lemma, makes Choice explicit, and rewrites the constants and details.

The sources state Stone's theorem that every metric space is paracompact. The item states the theorem with the Choice used by its chosen Ornstein proof made explicit and derives it from the two separately recorded construction lemmas.

Stone's theorem and the Hausdorff paracompact partition characterization semantically give the claim. The item exposes Choice/DC and records the immediate two-theorem composition rather than following a separate sourced proof.

Bacon's peer-reviewed paper proves the stronger standard result that a countably compact paracompact space is compact. The item adds Hausdorffness and Countable Choice to make its particular closed-discrete-subset proof valid in the library's explicit foundations, so the statement is a specialization. The detailed extraction proof is locally composed.

The sources state that every regular Lindelöf space is paracompact and use the same countable shrinking/difference construction. The item makes Countable Choice explicit and rewrites the indexing and least-index argument.

The sources explicitly require Hausdorffness for the normality theorem and note that, under the library's no-Hausdorff definition, compact nonnormal spaces are paracompact counterexamples. The item turns omission of that hypothesis into a false statement and supplies its own finite three-point witness.

The sources identify omega_1 as nonparacompact and give the ordinal compactness facts for omega_1 and omega_1+1 that make the standard open-in-compact obstruction to hereditary paracompactness. The item makes Choice explicit and packages the witness as a refutation with a local derivation.

The sources give the standard Sorgenfrey/lower-limit-line counterexample: each factor is paracompact, while its square is not normal and hence not paracompact Hausdorff. The item presents the erroneous universal product claim and spells out the contradiction under explicit Choice.

This is a genuinely page-specific synthesis rather than a recognizable literature proposition: it inventories this page's local no-Hausdorff convention and the exact Choice/DC expenditures of its own proofs. Each sentence was checked directly against the cited on-disk definitions, theorems, and the two Ornstein construction items.
Datchev's Purdue notes give rho(x)=max(1-|x|,0), its integer translates, the identity sum rho(x-n)=1, and the same support/local-finiteness verification. The item reproduces that construction.

The exact cover and clipped affine formulas at the bespoke thresholds 1/4, 1/3, 2/3, and 3/4 are a locally designed witness, not a recoverable named result. Direct substitution verifies continuity, phi+psi=1, support(phi)=[0,2/3] inside U, and support(psi)=[1/3,1] inside V.

The exact interval family is a bespoke elementary witness. Directly, the intervals (1/(n+1),1/n) are pairwise disjoint, so each point lies in at most one member, while every neighbourhood of 0 meets all sufficiently late members; this verifies point-finiteness and failure of local finiteness.

The exact triangular bumps on the bespoke adjacent intervals [1/(n+1),1/n] are a locally invented witness. The displayed formulas directly show disjoint cozero sets, pointwise finiteness, f(0)=0, c_n to 0, and f(c_n)=1, so discontinuity is elementary.

The Auburn notes state that omega_1 is not paracompact and develop the same ordinal-space context. The item records the standard countably compact/noncompact/Hausdorff contradiction with the library's Countable Choice and Choice hypotheses made explicit.

The standard counterexample is omega_1 as the open initial segment of compact omega_1+1, with omega_1 nonparacompact. The item restates it under explicit Choice and gives the short local verification from the cited ordinal facts.

The sources give the same lower-limit/Sorgenfrey-line factors and nonparacompact square. The item is a shortened counterexample pointing to the page's fully expanded false-statement refutation, with Choice explicit.
